summary: The ADVERSE verdict (85% confidence) is based on documented enforcement actions against Patagonia, Inc. within the last ten years: an EEOC settlement in 2019, a Seattle Office for Labour Standards fine and employee compensation in 2022 for violating the Secure Scheduling Ordinance, and an NLRB charge of unfair labor practices in 2020. These findings demonstrate a pattern of regulatory and labor‑law adverse conduct, supporting the adverse assessment despite the lack of sanctions listings or bankruptcy events.

findings.statement: Patagonia, Inc. settled an EEOC complaint in 2019, paying a settlement (amount unspecified).
Patagonia, Inc. was fined by the Seattle Office for Labour Standards in 2022 for violating the Secure Scheduling Ordinance, paying a fine and employee compensation.
Patagonia, Inc. faced an NLRB charge of unfair labor practices in 2020, which resulted in no financial fine.
Patagonia, Inc. agreed to pay nearly $55,000 to employees and a $575.31 fine to the City of Seattle for violating the Secure Scheduling law (2022).

gaps: Exact legal name, state of incorporation, and registration number of Patagonia, Inc. were not established in the provided evidence.
Whether Patagonia, Inc. appears on any government sanctions or denied parties lists (e.g., OFAC SDN, EU Consolidated List) could not be determined.
No information was found regarding bankruptcy, receivership, or insolvency proceedings for Patagonia, Inc. in any jurisdiction.
Precise monetary amount of the 2019 EEOC settlement was not disclosed in the sources.
Details of the NLRB charge outcome beyond the absence of a financial fine (e.g., any required remedial actions) were not provided.
Information about any adverse actions involving wholly-owned subsidiaries of Patagonia, Inc. was not present.
